text:
Kyle Palmieri is 35, played only 25 games last season, and Newsday has already asked why he has struggled to produce. Four goals and eight points in 22 games is a slow start for a player with 276 career goals. Our numbers say the explanation is mostly finishing. He has four goals on 6.7 expected (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and the Islanders take 56% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, seven points better than without him.

That is a player doing the work. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in a small sample, had him on the end of a lot of passes across the slot and from behind the net, the most dangerous looks there are. He is playing with Bo Horvat and Simon Holmstrom at morning skate. Our range has him around 20 goals. A Long Island native, he scored the go-ahead goal in Winnipeg last week. More should follow.
